summary: Independent review of the restart-evidence fix for inactive services. OPERATIONAL TOOLING ONLY; no trading code, no runtime path. THIS IS THE CHECKLIST DOING EXACTLY WHAT IT WAS BUILT FOR: #952's FIRST live pre-restart run surfaced a real blocker — a deliberately disabled tv-alerts unit had no ExecMainStartTimestamp, which made the whole checklist UNMEASURED. It found that before the restart rather than during it, which is the argument for running a new checklist against production the first chance you get. THE FIX IS CORRECTLY SHAPED AND IS NOT A BLANKET TOLERANCE: deliberately_inactive requires an explicit allowlist membership (INTENTIONALLY_INACTIVE_SERVICES, currently just tv-alerts) AND pid == 0 AND active_state == inactive AND sub_state == dead. Any service outside that allowlist, or inside it but in any other state, still raises EvidenceUnknown. THE SECOND CHANGE IS SUBTLY BETTER THAN WHAT IT REPLACED AND I WANT THAT RECORDED: untouched services were previously asserted to be active/running; they are now asserted to be UNCHANGED FROM THE PRE-RESTART SNAPSHOT — same pid, same active_state, same sub_state, same NRestarts. That is the correct predicate for RESTART EVIDENCE, which exists to prove we restarted what we meant to and left everything else alone. Health is fleet_health's job, not this tool's, and the old predicate would have failed a service that was deliberately inactive both before and after. MUTATIONS, the two that matter both RED: making the allowlist condition unconditional so ANY inactive service is tolerated fails test_required_service_without_a_start_timestamp_is_unmeasured; reverting the untouched check to require active fails test_report_accepts_a_deliberately_inactive_service_that_stays_unchanged. 25 focused tests pass. FINDING, NON-BLOCKING, AND I AM RECORDING IT RATHER THAN OMITTING IT: the pid == 0 and sub_state == dead conditions can EACH be deleted with all 25 tests green. No control covers an allowlisted service in an UNEXPECTED state — failed, or dead with a stale pid. I am not withholding on it for two reasons, both checked rather than assumed. First, the DANGEROUS direction is already controlled: test_report_fails_if_a_deliberately_inactive_service_starts catches a service we believed was off coming back on. Second, the uncovered path fails SAFE — an unexpected state makes deliberately_inactive false, started_raw is empty, and the code raises EvidenceUnknown, so the worst outcome is an UNMEASURED verdict and never a false pass. Worth one commit later, the same shape as the two #952 gaps codex closed in a single commit. Controlled full unit pair vs base 4e9db4df: base 46 failed / 3731 passed, head 46 failed / 3735 passed, ZERO new failure names and ZERO fixed, and I verified the base worktree actually existed before trusting the comparison this time. Ancestor PASS. Reviewer differs from the author. No blocking findings.
